diagnosis: The checks C1 and C3 passed because the lone decision-maker could rely on the publicly available facts S1 and S3, which were sufficient to justify the decisions made. Specifically, the settlements in all rollouts justified the decisions based on 'Inadequate handoff procedures and lack of clear guidelines for concurrent client escalations' (C1) and 'Inadequate handoff procedures and lack of clear expectations' (C3), both of which were supported by facts S1 and S3.

C1.why: The three firsthand handoffs change the finding from an apparent individual performance failure to a missing-input handoff-process problem, while Nora's prior agreement changes the support plan to a peer feedback partnership lasting exactly four weeks.

C3.why: The approved accommodation changes Nora's workload cap to exactly three concurrent client escalations and changes review preparation to written agendas and prompts exactly two business days in advance.
